Why do S waves never arrive beyond about 103° from a quake?

slides.reveal: Answer: A. S (shear) waves cannot travel through liquid, and the liquid outer core stops them, leaving a shadow zone beyond about 103 degrees from the quake (IRIS; slide 4).

Why are the magnetic stripes mirror images across a ridge?
New rock forms at the ridge and moves off both ways
The field flips on one side only

slides.reveal: Answer: A. As new crust forms at the ridge it records the direction of Earth's magnetic field; seafloor spreading then carries that strip away on both sides, so each reversal is recorded twice, as mirror-image stripes (Vine and Matthews 1963; USGS; slide 11).

Which boundary builds a volcanic island arc like the Aleutians?
Plates pull apart at a ridge

slides.reveal: Answer: A. When two oceanic plates converge, one subducts under the other, forming a trench and a curved chain of volcanic islands, an island arc, such as the Aleutians and the Marianas (USGS; slide 16).

How is the Wabash Valley zone different from the San Andreas?
It is inside a plate, on old buried faults
It is a transform plate boundary
Indiana sits on a subduction zone

slides.reveal: Answer: A. The Wabash Valley Seismic Zone is an intraplate zone: deeply buried normal faults inside the North American Plate, along an ancient failed rift (IGWS; slide 22).
